name: Elishama
overview: Elishama is a male figure noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Nethaniah. He is possibly from the tribe of Judah, as 2 Kings 25:25 describes him as being of the royal lineage, indicating a connection to the royal family. Beyond this, little else is recorded about his personal background or tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Elishama means "G-d has heard," reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Kings 25:25, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine attentiveness.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Elishama as the father of Nethaniah, as stated in 2 Kings 25:25. No other family relationships are explicitly recorded for him beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Elishama's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his status as a member of the royal family during a critical period in Judah's history, as implied by his being the father of Nethaniah. This connection situates him within the lineage associated with the monarchy of Judah, highlighting his role in the unfolding of God's providential plan for His people during the late kingdom era.
